# BAD-035 — Admin /scenes: last-imported and last-recorded columns, sortable

## Brief
Eric's ask (2026-09-14): in the admin dashboard's Scenes page, add a column showing the last imported datetime and the last users-recorded datetime, so the table can also be sorted by the scenes most recently used or imported.

Where it lives: `admin/src/lib/scenes.ts` builds the list query (CTEs `acquired`, `recorded`, `scenes`, with `SORTS` naming the sortable columns) and `admin/src/app/scenes/page.tsx` renders the table with a `Th` header per sort key. The detail page at `admin/src/app/scenes/[name]/page.tsx` already renders per-account `acquiredAt` and `lastTakeAt` with `Time` / `TimeAgo` from `admin/src/components/Time.tsx` and `relative` from `admin/src/lib/format.ts`; the list should render the same way.

Shape:
- `acq` gains `max(created_at) as last_imported_at`; `rec` gains `max(created_at) as last_recorded_at`; `scenes` carries both through the full outer join (null when that side has no rows in the window).
- `SceneRow` gains `lastImportedAt: string | null` and `lastRecordedAt: string | null`.
- `SORTS` gains `last_imported` and `last_recorded`; the existing `nulls last, title asc` tiebreak applies.
- Two new `Th` columns after "Users recorded" (or beside "Imported" / "Users recorded" if that reads better): "Last imported" and "Last recorded", each `TimeAgo` with the exact UTC time on hover, an em dash when null. `colSpan` on the empty row grows to match.
- Both timestamps are "within the selected window", the same as every other number on the row; a scene acquired before the window shows a dash for last imported, like the detail page's "had it already".

Constraints from admin/CLAUDE.md: still exactly one query per render (no second round trip); the aggregates ride the same scan the counts already do. Both tables already have a bare `(created_at desc)` index.

Proof: `cd admin && npm run verify` (typecheck, lint, build, check:standalone, check:secrets) green, plus `npm test` at the root green, with a new `test/server/admin-scenes-list.test.mjs` pinning, in the shape of `admin-accounts-list.test.mjs`, that `SORTS` names both keys, that the page renders a `Th` for each, and that `listScenes` maps both fields.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus: two SQL aggregates, two table columns, two sort keys and a source-pinning test in test/server/. Verified by admin verify (typecheck, lint, build) plus npm test.
